handbookNote: New York Real Estate Broker license upgrade exam, administered directly by the New York State Department of State (DOS), Division of Licensing Services -- unlike most other states, New York has no third-party testing vendor (no PSI/Pearson VUE/Prometric); the qualifying exam is scheduled through eAccessNY and given at DOS testing centers. Mechanics CONFIRMED directly from dos.ny.gov's own official pages (dos.ny.gov/become-real-estate-broker and dos.ny.gov/real-estate-broker-frequently-asked-questions, fetched and read directly): a 2 1/2-hour (150-minute) written exam, reported strictly as pass/fail with no numerical score, a $15 exam fee, a passing result valid for 2 years, and a $185 initial license application fee. DOS does NOT publish an exact item count or passing percentage for the broker exam (consistent with its pass/fail-only reporting policy) -- the commonly-cited '100 questions / 70% passing' figures found on third-party test-prep sites are NOT DOS-confirmed and are flagged as hedges within the question bank rather than presented as fact. Experience/education prerequisites CONFIRMED from the same DOS pages: at least 2 years' experience as a licensed real estate salesperson, OR at least 3 years' general real estate field experience, or a qualifying combination, plus 152 total hours of DOS-approved qualifying education (the 45-hour salesperson course + a 75-hour broker course + a 32-hour supplemental broker curriculum). The specific 3,500/5,250-point experience-chart thresholds and the 250-point/25-point per-transaction values are well-corroborated across licensing-industry sources but were not independently verified against a pinpoint-cited DOS PDF in this pass, and are flagged as hedges in-content. Real statute/rule citations used throughout and independently verified via law.cornell.edu, nysenate.gov, justia.com, and dos.ny.gov in this research pass include: RPL Article 12-A Sections 440 (definitions), 440-a (entity/individual licensing), 441-a (license, pocket card, office sign), 441-c (discipline -- untrustworthiness/incompetency/fraud, confirmed via DOS Legal Memorandum LI01), 442/442-a (splitting commissions; salesperson compensation only from supervising broker), 442-d (license prerequisite to sue for commission), 442-e (misdemeanor penalties, 1x-4x commission, AG prosecution, subpoena power), 443 (agency disclosure -- DOS Form 1736, first substantive contact, dual agency with designated sales agents), and 294-b (Commission Escrow Act); 19 NYCRR Part 175 Sections 175.1 (escrow/anti-commingling -- 3-business-day deposit, separate federally-insured account, interest-handling rule), 175.19 (net listings prohibited -- a notable contrast with states that permit them), 175.20 (branch offices), 175.21 (broker supervision standard -- 'regular, frequent and consistent' oversight, salesperson recordkeeping), 175.23 (3-year transaction record retention), and 175.25 (advertising/team-name rules); RPAPL Sections 768/853 (self-help eviction prohibition, statewide, class A misdemeanor, treble damages), 1303/1304/1306/1331 (foreclosure notice and lis pendens requirements); RPL Section 226-c and GOL Section 7-108(1-a) (HSTPA 2019 statewide tenant protections -- graduated 30/60/90-day rent-increase/non-renewal notice, one-month security deposit cap, 14-day itemized deposit return); RPL Article 14 Sections 460-467 (Property Condition Disclosure Act, AS AMENDED effective March 20, 2024 -- eliminating the prior $500 opt-out credit and adding 7 new flood-disclosure questions, expanding the DOS-1614-f form from 49 to 56 questions, independently verified via nysar.com and nysba.org coverage of the 2023 Hochul-signed amendment); Executive Law Section 296(5) (NY Human Rights Law, including the 2019 addition of 'lawful source of income' as a protected class, and a hedged note on a 2023 trial-level ruling questioning that provision's application to Section 8 vouchers); RPL Article 9 Section 291 (race-notice recording statute) and General Obligations Law Section 5-703 (statute of frauds); and New York-specific finance/tax content -- the mortgage recording tax and CEMA refinance mechanism (NY Tax Law Section 255), NY's judicial (not non-judicial) foreclosure process, the NYS real estate transfer tax ($2/$500) and mansion tax (1%+ on $1M+ residential, with an enhanced NYC tier above $3M effective 7/1/2019), and the STAR school-tax-relief program. Per the user's brief that broker content should go substantially deeper than the existing ny_real_estate (salesperson) track into broker-specific supervision, escrow, and office-management territory, this 299-question bank concentrates its heaviest volume (over 100 of 299 questions, roughly 34%) into five broker-specific buckets: Broker Office Management/Branch Offices/Recordkeeping, Broker Supervision of Salespersons & Associate Brokers, Escrow & Trust Fund Management, Commission/Compensation & Broker-Salesperson Relationships, and License Law/DOS Discipline/Investigations/CE -- content largely absent from the sales-agent-tier track. Deed types (bargain and sale with covenant against grantor's acts, quitclaim, full covenant and warranty), New York's 'attorney state' closing custom (with DOS's own Legal Memorandum LI04 on unauthorized practice of law used to ground the attorney-approval-clause safe harbor and the limits on brokers drafting legal terms), and standard appraisal-theory/real-estate-math/general-contract-law content not tied to a single New York statute are flagged in-content with source_note 'hedge: standard...' or 'hedge: well-corroborated...' language, consistent with this project's grounding standard -- never presented as pinpoint-cited New York statute where they are not. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized going rate for Real Estate tracks (applied project-wide since 2026-08-13), consistent with ny_real_estate.json, ca_re_broker.json, tx_re_broker.json, and fl_re_broker.json. Answer choices were drafted correct-as-choice_a throughout, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_ny_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all questions in file order, not manual).
